summary: Audit of what the owner reads and whether the documents are true, done in a scratch copy (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude-Brain/c34b258b-1734-5756-8764-15f4f3352652/scratchpad/owner-docs) with its remotes cut before any pushing command; nothing was written to /home/user/Claude-Brain. The engine's measured claims mostly hold (407 tests at 19fb016 and 410 at 9e4b158, doctor healthy, lint 0 errors, 100 templates, HR held-out 78/86 recomputed, routing 107/107 recomputed, 12 eval tasks sound). The weak side is the owner path. (1) The promise he relies on most, "Continue picks up exactly where the last chat stopped", fails in a reproduced case: the last chat pushes its checkpoint to its own branch, a new chat starts from main (CLAUDE_CODE_BASE_REF=main), boot does not look at other branches, and handover still said "ready". The STATUS.md on the repository front page is stale for the same reason. (2) The owner files contradict each other and GitHub: the guide says a red cross means do not merge while NEEDS_YOU says every push shows a red cross (live: the latest 5 of 37 runs failed in 3 seconds), no pull request has ever existed although the guide's undo story depends on one, and the click path for protecting main creates a ruleset that is disabled by default and, on a private repository, needs a paid plan nobody checked. (3) Two things he is told he can do on GitHub are not read reliably: OVERTURNED is never surfaced by any script, and RESOLVED is matched as a substring (an item whose text contains "resolved" vanishes from STATUS; "RESUELTO" is ignored). (4) In a brain-only chat, which this session is, "Status" and "Hand over" have no engine support (exit 1). (5) Numbers are restated by hand in five documents and have drifted (tests: 310+, 358, 406, 407 against 410; build cost: $123, $162 against the ledger's $175.49); lint does not cover docs/ or numbers. (6) Generated STATUS.md is short and honest but shows no address to open, uses a machine timestamp and English labels even for a project created with --language es (the field is never read). (7) Several phrases the owner is told to type are not recognised by route or any skill ("Check the brain", "HR report", "Consolidate", "schedule the weekly learning run"), and his real opening message today was sized "1 small task, data". The guide lacks: what to do when a chat dies, where to see the result, click paths for merging, and Spanish for six of nine phrases.
strengths: Generated STATUS.md is short and built only from state and logs: 23 to 29 lines in the scratch project, with next items, open owner items and the list-price caveat; boot stays far under its cap (819 bytes with a project, 861 brain-only, cap 1,500). Any redesign must keep it script-generated and under one phone screen.

The measured claims that matter were reproduced exactly: HR held-out selection 78 first / 86 top three of 100, routing tier 107 of 107, eval audit 12 sound, 100 templates in 10 groups, 141 items valid, doctor healthy, lint 0 errors. BUILD_STATUS and REQUIREMENTS use honest statuses (met / reframed / live) and an 'Open, with reasons' table; keep that structure.

Handover refuses to say 'ready' while either repository has uncommitted or unpushed work (seen: exit 1 with 'brain: branch ... has never been pushed'), commits its own note, and prints one line to paste. The fix for the branch problem should build on this, not replace it.

NEEDS_YOU items follow one shape (Why / How / Meanwhile) with bold click targets and 'work never waits'; open items are counted in boot ('needs owner: N') and listed in STATUS.md. A repository created on GitHub with only README, LICENSE or .gitignore is treated as empty, and init is idempotent.

The core Spanish phrases are recognised with or without accents and inverted marks: Nuevo proyecto, Empieza, Continúa/Continua, Sigue, Rápido/Rapido, A fondo, Estado, ¿Cómo vamos?, Pasa a un chat nuevo, Prepara el relevo, ¿Qué has aprendido?, Vuelve atrás, Deshaz eso, Para después de esto.

findings.title: "Continue" in a new chat resumes an old checkpoint and handover still says ready: state is pushed to the last chat's branch, a new chat starts from main, and boot does not look
findings.evidence: NEEDS_YOU.md:7 states the platform fact: "a new chat starts from each repository's `main` branch". This session confirms it: env CLAUDE_CODE_BASE_REF=main, and the reflog shows "checkout: moving from 19fb016 to claude/optimistic-newton-sh6lcx". engine/state.py:172-176 pushes the checkpoint to the current branch only. `grep -n "branch\|fetch\|origin" engine/detect.py` prints nothing: boot never looks at other branches. Reproduced in the scratch project: on branch claude/session-a, `brain checkpoint --done "Pantalla para añadir un gasto" --item "Resumen mensual" --push` printed "checkpoint pushed to claude/session-a"; `brain handover` printed "ready: both repositories are committed and pushed ... paste in a new chat with both repositories attached:  Continue" (exit 0). Fresh clone of the default branch (what a new chat gets), then `brain boot "Continue"` printed "item: Pantalla para añadir un gasto · last done: Proyecto creado y plan escrito" while `git show origin/claude/session-a:.brain/STATE.md` holds "item: Resumen mensual / last_done: Pantalla para añadir un gasto". No warning. The STATUS.md in that clone (what GitHub shows on the repository front page) was the old one too. CB-104 lists this flow as needing a live session; this is the concrete failing case and it needs no live session to reproduce.
findings.repro: S=<scratch>; in a managed project with a bare remote whose HEAD is main: git checkout -b claude/session-a; python3 $S/brain/bin/brain checkpoint --done A --item B --push; python3 $S/brain/bin/brain handover; git clone <remote> $S/chat2/proj (next to a copy of the brain); cd $S/chat2/proj; python3 ../brain/bin/brain boot "Continue"  -> shows item A as in progress, not B.
findings.proposed_fix: 1) engine/state.py: add newer_checkpoint(project): unless BRAIN_NO_NETWORK=1, run `git fetch -q origin '+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*'` with a 6-second timeout (a failure is ignored), then for each refs/remotes/origin/* read `.brain/STATE.md` with `git show` and return (ref, updated, item) for the latest `updated:` that is later than the local one. A 15-line prototype of this found ('origin/claude/session-a', '2026-11-10T17:50:48Z', 'Resumen mensual') in the reproduced case. 2) engine/detect.py boot_lines: print it straight after the mode line so the byte cap never drops it: `WARNING: newer checkpoint on origin/claude/session-a (2026-11-10 17:50, item: Resumen mensual): merge that branch into this one, then run boot again`. 3) .claude/skills/brain-start/SKILL.md, under Orient: "If boot warns of a newer checkpoint on another branch, the last chat's work is there: a new chat starts from the default branch and the last chat pushed to its own. Merge that branch into this session's branch (`git merge origin/<branch>`), run `BRAIN boot` again, and only then resume." 4) engine/state.py handover and cmd_status: print one more line, `latest STATUS.md: https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/blob/<branch>/STATUS.md` (from `git remote get-url origin` and the branch), and brain-handover / brain-status 'Tell the owner': "Give him that link: between releases the newest STATUS.md is on this chat's branch, not on the repository's front page." 5) OWNER_GUIDE.md, 'The three files you read', add: "Between releases the newest copy of these files is on the chat's own branch, so open them from the link Claude gives at the end of each report, not from the repository's front page."
findings.acceptance: New test in tests/test_hygiene.py, test_boot_warns_when_a_newer_checkpoint_is_on_another_branch: bare remote with main (item A) and claude/x (later `updated:`, item B); clone the default branch; boot_lines("Continue") contains "newer checkpoint on origin/claude/x"; after `git merge origin/claude/x` the warning is gone and the item line shows B. `python3 -m unittest tests.test_hygiene` OK; boot output stays under 1,500 bytes (existing cap test).

findings.title: The guide says a red cross means do not merge, NEEDS_YOU says every push shows a red cross, and the pull-request undo story has no instance: he cannot follow both, and learning only counts what reaches main
findings.evidence: OWNER_GUIDE.md:64 "A check named **brain** also runs on GitHub for every change to the brain; a red cross on a pull request means do not merge it yet." NEEDS_YOU.md:47 "a red cross will show on every push even though nothing is wrong". Live (GitHub connector, list_workflow_runs): total_count 37; runs 33 to 37 all conclusion "failure", each created and finished within 3 seconds (for example created 17:50:09Z, updated 17:50:12Z), on main and on both claude/ branches. OWNER_GUIDE.md:60 "Claude opens each learning change as one pull request ... To undo a merged one, open that pull request and press **Revert**"; list_pull_requests with state=all returned []. `git log --oneline main..HEAD` shows the first real learning change (790084d "learn: first real consolidation (delta d-20261110-a431e755f2 ...)") sitting on the session branch between an engine fix (30086dc) and a docs commit (2ea9316), so it cannot become one pull request with its own Revert button. .claude/skills/brain-learn/SKILL.md:16 "consolidation only sees what has reached `main`". Read literally today: every learning pull request is red, so none is merged, so nothing is learned.
findings.proposed_fix: OWNER_GUIDE.md, replace the last sentence of 'If something seems broken' with: "A check named **brain** is meant to run on GitHub for every change to the brain. Until item 7 in NEEDS_YOU.md is done GitHub does not start it, so every change shows a red cross that says nothing about the change. Until then, read the line in the pull request that begins 'Checks run in the session:' and merge when it says they passed. Once item 7 is done, a red cross means do not merge yet." OWNER_GUIDE.md 'Undoing something the brain learned', add the clicks: "To keep one: github.com → **Claude-Brain** → **Pull requests** → open the one Claude named → **Merge pull request** → **Confirm merge**. To undo one: **Pull requests** → **Closed** → open it → **Revert** → **Create pull request** → **Merge pull request**." .claude/skills/brain-learn/SKILL.md 'Consolidate', add: "Commit the delta alone on a branch named `learn/<delta id>` cut from `main`, and open one pull request for it: a learning change mixed with other commits has no Revert button of its own. Put the gate result in the pull request text as a line beginning 'Checks run in the session:' (test count and each command's exit code): until GitHub's check can start it is the only evidence he has." engine/learn.py: after consolidate, print that next step with the branch name. For this session: move delta d-20261110-a431e755f2 to its own branch and pull request before the engineering commits go to main.
findings.acceptance: `grep -c "red cross on a pull request means do not merge it yet" OWNER_GUIDE.md` is 0; `python3 bin/brain lint` exits 0; `python3 bin/brain learn consolidate` in a scratch copy prints a line containing `learn/d-`; on GitHub one pull request exists whose changed files are only under learning/, stats/, memory/, owner/, playbooks/.

findings.title: NEEDS_YOU.md: the clicks for protecting main create a ruleset that is disabled by default and may need a paid plan; the resolved item is shown first with stale steps; the real blocker is last
findings.evidence: NEEDS_YOU.md:17 "**Settings** → **Branches** → **Add branch ruleset** (or **Add rule**) → branch name `main` → tick ... → **Create**". GitHub's own page (docs.github.com, 'Creating rulesets for a repository', fetched today) gives: Settings → Rules → Rulesets → New ruleset → New branch ruleset → name → "Optionally, to change the default enforcement status, click **Disabled** and select an enforcement status" → "**Disabled:** your ruleset will not be enforced" → Target branches: Add a target. The file's steps have no enforcement step and no target step, so following them yields a ruleset that does nothing while everyone believes main is protected. GitHub's plans page (fetched today) lists "Protected branches" among the features GitHub Pro adds for private repositories; list_repos returns visibility "private" for this repository; list_branches returns "protected": false for main. Nothing in NEEDS_YOU.md or D-12 checks the plan, and item 4A (auto-merge) depends on item 2. Presentation: NEEDS_YOU.md:5-12 shows item 1 in full, with click steps naming the old branch `claude/wizardly-darwin-91m4pl`, and only its last line says RESOLVED; item 2's title says "after items 1 and 7"; :18 says "310+ tests" (410 now); :41 says "after item 1 is done" (it is); item 7, which blocks 2 and 4A, is at the bottom; items 3 and 5 ask for nothing he can click or reply. Item numbers are referenced from docs/DECISIONS.md:18, docs/REQUIREMENTS.md:11, docs/BUILD_STATUS.md:79 and :81, docs/NEXT_SESSION.md:30, so they should stay stable.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep the numbers; change the text. Line 3, add: "Do them in this order: 7, then 2, then 4. Item 6 can be done now." Item 1 becomes one line: "## 1. Done: the built brain is on `main`" followed by "RESOLVED: 2026-11-10, you approved it in chat." (steps removed). Item 2: title "## 2. Protect the brain's `main` (5 minutes, after item 7)"; add "- **First check:** this repository is private, and GitHub enforces branch rules on a private repository only on a paid personal plan. github.com → your picture → **Settings** → **Billing and licensing**: it shows **Free** or **Pro**. On Free, tell me and I will lay out the two choices (upgrade, or keep the check as advice only)."; replace How with "github.com → **javilfr/Claude-Brain** → **Settings** → **Rules** → **Rulesets** → **New ruleset** → **New branch ruleset**. Name it `main`. Change **Enforcement status** from **Disabled** to **Active**: a disabled ruleset does nothing. **Target branches** → **Add target** → **Include default branch**. Tick **Require a pull request before merging** and **Require status checks to pass**, then **Add checks**, type `brain` and pick it. **Create**."; add "- **How you know it worked:** say 'check the protection' and I will read the rules GitHub reports for `main`."; Meanwhile: "... The same checks pass when run inside a session (counts are in `docs/BUILD_STATUS.md`)." Item 6: drop "after item 1 is done,". Item 3: move its text to OWNER_GUIDE.md step 3 (already there) and leave "## 3. Nothing to do: the model habit moved to the owner guide" with a RESOLVED line. Item 5: title "## 5. Nothing to do yet: optional guards in two-repo chats" and one line saying Claude will add clicks when ticket CB-106 is tested.
findings.acceptance: In a copy: python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'.'); from pathlib import Path; from engine import state; print(state.open_needs(Path('.')))" lists exactly items 2, 4, 6, 7; `grep -c "wizardly-darwin\|310+" NEEDS_YOU.md` is 0; `grep -c "Enforcement status" NEEDS_YOU.md` is 1; after the owner does item 2, `gh api repos/javilfr/Claude-Brain/rules/branches/main` returns a non-empty list.

findings.title: An OVERTURNED decision is never surfaced by any script, so "the next chat applies it" depends on the lead reading the whole decisions file; three files give three different instructions
findings.evidence: OWNER_GUIDE.md:38 "To reverse one, edit the line on GitHub and write **OVERTURNED** with what you want instead. The next chat applies it." `grep -rn OVERTURNED engine/` returns nothing; the only mechanism is one sentence in .claude/skills/brain-start/SKILL.md:23, while the same skill says of boot "do not re-read what it printed" and CLAUDE.md rule 3 says scripts before reading. Test in the scratch project: appended to .brain/DECISIONS.md a decision row and the line "OVERTURNED: quiero que se guarde en la nube con mi cuenta de Google"; `brain boot "Continue"` and `brain resume` printed the usual lines with no mention of it; `brain validate` said "contract v1 valid". Wording differs: the guide says edit the line; contract/template/.brain/DECISIONS.md:3 says "write `OVERTURNED:` and what you want instead on the line below it, or say so in chat"; docs/DECISIONS.md:3 says "write `OVERTURNED:` under the row". The decisions are a Markdown table: a line typed under a row splits the table on GitHub, and on a phone each row is one very long raw line to edit.
findings.proposed_fix: engine/state.py: add overturned(project) returning the lines of .brain/DECISIONS.md that contain OVERTURNED (any case; also REVERTIDA and ANULADA) and do not end with `(applied <date>)`. engine/detect.py boot_lines and state.resume_lines: when the list is not empty print `overturned: N decision(s) he reversed in .brain/DECISIONS.md are not applied yet: apply them before resuming`. STATUS.md: one line "- Reversed by you, not applied yet: N". .claude/skills/brain-start/SKILL.md: "When boot reports overturned decisions, apply each one, then add `(applied <date>)` to the end of his line so it is reported once." One wording in all three places (template, OWNER_GUIDE.md:38, docs/DECISIONS.md:3): "To reverse one, say so in chat (for example 'reverse decision 3: use euros'), or on GitHub add a line at the end of this file: `OVERTURNED 3:` and what you want instead. Claude applies it at the start of the next chat and marks it applied." The frozen fixture evals/fixtures/project-v1 keeps the old sentence; the reader accepts both forms.
findings.acceptance: New test in tests/test_core.py: a project whose DECISIONS.md ends with "OVERTURNED 1: store in the cloud" gives boot_lines containing "overturned: 1"; after appending "(applied 2026-11-11)" to that line the boot line is absent. `grep -c "line below it\|under the row\|edit the line on GitHub" OWNER_GUIDE.md docs/DECISIONS.md contract/template/.brain/DECISIONS.md` gives 0 for each; tests/test_fixtures.py still passes.

findings.title: RESOLVED is matched as a substring: an open item whose text contains "resolved" vanishes from STATUS.md and from boot's count, and "RESUELTO" or "Hecho" is ignored
findings.evidence: engine/state.py:254 `elif "RESOLVED" in line.upper(): resolved = True`. Scratch project NEEDS_YOU.md with four items: 1 open; 2 open, with the Why line "until the domain name is resolved by DNS to Vercel, the address is the long vercel.app one"; 3 answered by the owner with "RESUELTO: verde"; 4 answered with "Hecho, ya está guardada." `brain status` printed under Needs you: "- 1. Connect Vercel (3 minutes)", "- 3. Elige el color principal", "- 4. Stripe key"; `brain boot` printed "needs owner: 3". Item 2, which is open, is missing; items 3 and 4, which he answered in Spanish, still show as open. He often writes in Spanish (owner/standing.jsonl own-reply-language cites 4+ sessions).
findings.repro: In a managed project append the four items above to NEEDS_YOU.md, then run `python3 <brain>/bin/brain status`.
findings.proposed_fix: engine/state.py: replace the substring test with a line-start match, `RESOLVED_LINE = re.compile(r"^\s*(?:[-*>]\s*)?\**\s*(RESOLVED|RESUELTO|RESUELTA|HECHO|LISTO)\b", re.I)` and `elif RESOLVED_LINE.match(line): resolved = True`. contract/template/NEEDS_YOU.md line 3 (a new optional wording, no contract bump): "Reply in chat, or write `RESOLVED:` (or `RESUELTO:`) on a line of its own under an item." Same sentence in the brain's NEEDS_YOU.md:3 and OWNER_GUIDE.md:44.
findings.acceptance: Extend tests/test_core.py (the test around line 275) with the four-item file: open_needs returns exactly the titles of items 1 and 2. `python3 -m unittest tests.test_core` OK.

findings.title: In a chat with only the brain attached, "Status" and "Hand over" have no engine support (exit 1), the brain's own open owner items are not shown, and the handover note and ticket states are kept by hand
findings.evidence: In a folder holding only a clone of the brain at 9e4b158: `python3 bin/brain status` printed "no managed project found (attach one, or run: brain init <path>)", exit 1; `python3 bin/brain handover` printed the same, exit 1. Both skills (brain-status, brain-handover) rest on those two commands. `brain boot "Status"` printed the mode line, "brain work: 10 open ticket(s) in docs/plan/tickets.json · next: CB-200 Baseline and self-audit" and the handover pointer, but nothing about the brain's NEEDS_YOU.md, although state.open_needs on the brain root returns six open items. docs/plan/tickets.json still has CB-200 and CB-201 as "open" while commits 790084d and 2ea9316 carry "Brain-Bootstrap: CB-200 CB-201" and docs/BUILD_STATUS.md records their results, so the next brain-only boot would send a new chat back to CB-200; `brain plan --help` offers only schedule, assign and packet, so tickets are marked by editing JSON. docs/NEXT_SESSION.md is hand-written and already stale in the session it was written for (:8 "407 tests", 410 now; :11 "three unconsolidated records", consolidated in 790084d; :25 "$162", the ledger says $175.49). This session is brain-only and the owner opened it from his phone (CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=remote_mobile).
findings.proposed_fix: engine/state.py cmd_status, when no project is attached: print at most 12 lines about the brain itself and exit 0: version; branch and how many commits are not on main; open tickets and the next one; needs you (open item numbers from the brain's NEEDS_YOU.md via open_needs(BRAIN_ROOT)); inbox files waiting for consolidation; this chat's list-price cost from the ledger. cmd_handover, when no project is attached: regenerate a block between `<!-- state:begin -->` and `<!-- state:end -->` in docs/NEXT_SESSION.md from the same data, check the brain is committed and pushed, and print "paste in a new chat with only Claude-Brain attached:  Continue". engine/detect.py brain_work_lines: add "needs owner: N" when the brain's NEEDS_YOU.md has open items. engine/schedule.py: add `brain plan done <file> <id>` so a ticket is closed by a command. engine/lint.py: a ticket id named in a `Brain-Bootstrap:` trailer on this branch must not be `open` in docs/plan/tickets.json. Skills: brain-status and brain-handover each get one sentence, "With only the brain attached, the same command reports on the brain itself."
findings.acceptance: In a folder holding only the brain: `python3 bin/brain status; echo $?` prints a line starting "needs you:" and 0; `python3 bin/brain handover; echo $?` prints the paste line and 0 when the tree is clean and pushed, and names the problem otherwise; `python3 bin/brain plan done docs/plan/tickets.json CB-200` then `python3 bin/brain boot` no longer names CB-200 as next; new tests in tests/test_hygiene.py for both modes.

findings.title: Generated STATUS.md does not say what to open, starts with a machine timestamp and a stage name, and stays in English for a project created with --language es (the field is never read)
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md:38 "For an app, done means deployed and visible on his phone; say what to look at." Set release.live_url to https://gastos.example.app and logged a release in .brain/log/releases.jsonl, then `brain status --full | grep -i "gastos.example\|release\|live"` matched nothing (exit 1): write_status (engine/state.py:287-320) never reads live_url or the release log. First lines as generated: "# Status: Gastos" then "Updated 2026-11-10T17:50:48Z · stage: build". The project was created with `brain init ... --language es` (project.json "languages": ["es"]) and its items were written in Spanish, yet every label is English ("Working on", "Last finished", "Needs you", "Cost"); `grep -n "languages" engine/*.py` shows the field is only written (contract.py:75, :311), never read, and contract/v1.schema.json gives it no meaning. Cost line: "Last session: about $4.36 at list prices, 44,911 output tokens, 1 helper(s)", while OWNER_GUIDE.md:50 says STATUS.md shows "tokens used"; the short `brain status` view cuts off at 14 lines before "Project to date".

findings.title: Three engine commands commit and push whatever is in learning/inbox to the origin of whichever copy of the brain they run from; today test records reached the real branch that way
findings.evidence: engine/state.py:190-203 (push_brain_records): `git add -- learning/inbox learning/radar`, commit "learn: session records", `git push -q -u origin <branch>`, with no check of which session wrote the files or where the copy lives; it is called by `checkpoint --push` and `handover`. A copy made with `cp -a` keeps the real remote: `git remote -v` in my copy printed "origin https://github.com/javilfr/Claude-Brain (push)" until I repointed it. On the real branch: commit 89b5624 "learn: session records" added learning/inbox/2026-11-10-------------tmp-evil.jsonl, 2026-11-10-timing-test.jsonl and a second copy of this session's record; commit 9e4b158 removed them ("three test records an auditor's scratch copy pushed by mistake (two with made-up session ids, one stale copy of this session's record)"). docs/BUILD_STATUS.md:48 already lists "forged inbox records are not distinguishable from real ones" as open; this is the cheap part of that problem and it happened within an hour of real use. Any helper that copies the brain to experiment has the same path.
findings.proposed_fix: engine/state.py push_brain_records: 1) commit only files this session wrote: `learning/inbox/<date>-<this session id>.jsonl`, `learning/inbox/<date>-radar.jsonl` and `learning/radar/state.json`; any other new inbox file is left uncommitted and named in the message ("left alone: 2026-11-10-timing-test.jsonl was not written by this session"). 2) Refuse to push when the brain's folder is under the system temporary directory or a path containing `/scratchpad/`, with the message "not pushed: this copy of the brain is a scratch copy"; the tests that need a push set BRAIN_ALLOW_SCRATCH_PUSH=1. 3) hr/GUIDELINES.md, one line for every brief whose task says to copy the brain: "If you copy the brain to experiment, run `git remote remove origin` in the copy first: `checkpoint --push`, `handover` and `release` push to the copy's origin."
findings.acceptance: New tests in tests/test_hygiene.py: with an inbox file named for another session beside this session's file, push_brain_records commits only this session's file and its message names the other; with the brain under a temporary folder and no override, it returns "not pushed: this copy of the brain is a scratch copy" and the bare remote has no new commit.

Of thirteen reporting commands tried in a clean clone (hr report, ml report, learn status, learn digest, budget, doctor, lint, recall, route, boot, hr rack, status, ledger) only `learn digest` left a change.

findings.title: Idea: a command that writes and closes NEEDS_YOU items, so every item has the same checked shape
findings.evidence: Items are written by hand (`brain --help` has no command for them); the shape Why / How / Meanwhile and "Nothing here needs a command" (contract/template/NEEDS_YOU.md:3) are prose only; the brain's own file drifted (resolved item first, non-actions listed, wrong click path). findings.proposed_fix: `brain needs add --title T --why W --how H --meanwhile M [--minutes N]` appends the next numbered item and refuses a How with no bold click target or with a code fence; `brain needs resolve N --answer "his words"` writes the RESOLVED line and moves the item under a `## Done` heading as one line; `brain needs list` prints open items. Numbers are never reused, so references stay valid.
